headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum split, and whales moving coins to cold storage while stablecoins pile onto exchanges.
paragraphs: The regime is decidedly bearish. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none of the seven assets show a golden cross (the 50-day crossing above the 200-day). This is a clean bearish setup: the intermediate trend is down across the board. Bitcoin sits 49 percent below its 12-month high, Ethereum 60.6 percent down, Solana 70.4 percent down, ADA 83.2 percent down, and XRP 67.7 percent down. The breadth here is total. Bitcoin has fallen 2.97 percent over the last 30 days and is down 1.59 percent over the last week. Ethereum, alone among the majors, is up 6.36 percent on the month and 1.81 percent on the week, a lone divergence that stands out; it remains well below its long-term trend line, so the move is a rebound within a downtrend, not a reversal signal.

Momentum readings show hesitation and mixed signals. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, neutral and slightly soft, while its MACD is below its signal line: the trend is still lower and not yet showing early acceleration. Ethereum's RSI is 56.3, the highest among the majors, yet its MACD is also below signal, which means price is holding better than momentum suggests. Solana's RSI is 42.7 and MACD below signal, consistent with the downtrend. XRP at 42.9 RSI and below-signal MACD is the weakest. Two outliers appear: BNB and DOGE both have MACD above their signal lines, which says their momentum has turned upward relative to trend, even though both remain below the 200-day line. This is a small tail of upside energy in the lower end of the cap table, not yet confirmed by price recapture of those averages. Volatility is elevated, with 30-day realized vol at 31.5 percent for Bitcoin, 45.4 percent for Ethereum, and 42 to 73 percent across the rest of the stack, a sign that price discovery is active and uncertain.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowded leverage and asymmetric liquidation risk. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding is negative (annualized at negative 1.8 percent), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold; open interest is 1.98 billion USD, a substantial size. The long-to-short ratio is 1.27, favoring longs. In the last 24 hours, Bitcoin liquidations totaled 7.5 million USD, with shorts accounting for 6.5 million of that: the short side is being flushed. Ethereum tells a sharper story: funding is positive at 0.003 percent per 8 hours (3.3 percent annualized), longs are paying, open interest is 1.29 billion USD, and the long-to-short ratio is 1.69, very long-heavy. Ethereum liquidations in 24 hours were 14 million USD, with shorts liquidated at 10.9 million and longs at 3.1 million, again a short-squeeze flavor. Solana shows extreme long skew at a 2.57 long-to-short ratio, positive funding at 2.3 percent annualized, and 125 liquidations, mostly shorts. XRP stands out inverted: its long-to-short is 3.28 (the most lopsidedly long of all), but funding is negative 8.1 percent annualized, which means longs are paying heavily to hold that position. The positioning is crowded and expensive on the long side across the board, with funding costs rising on the long books; short squeezes are clearing weak liquidation, but the cost of holding longs is rising.

Whale flows and stablecoin dynamics paint a picture of divergent behavior. Over the last 24 hours, 297.9 million USD in net Bitcoin moved off exchanges into cold storage, a classic flight-to-security move by large holders. The weekly trend for stablecoin flows into exchanges has been positive for two of the last four weeks (1.21 billion and 1.12 billion USD net inflows), but the biggest single move in the past 24 hours shows 789.5 million USD in USDT moving onto Binance and Bitfinex. This is dry powder staging: the whales are stashing coins while fresh stablecoins flow in, a setup that typically precedes either a capitulation dump or a reversal. The stablecoin float itself is 305.9 billion USD, down just 1.17 percent over 30 days, so the cash is not being deployed aggressively; it is accumulating on the sidelines. Spot Bitcoin ETF flows are consistent: 211.5 million USD net on the latest date (4 August 2026) and 381.4 million over the last five sessions. This is genuine traditional-finance bid, and it is steady, not frantic.

Sentiment is locked in fear (27 on the Fear & Greed Index, within a 30-day range of 20 to 33), yet the tape shows a more complex picture. The crowd is fearful, liquidation activity is flushing shorts, and majors are below their long-term lines, which normally compounds the fear. However, whales are moving coins to cold storage (a baiting or conviction move), ETF inflows persist day after day (patient real-money entry), and the stablecoin float is building without being deployed (dry powder accumulation). The contradiction between sentiment and positioning is the primary tension: the fear is genuine, but the money-flow picture suggests some players believe the washout is creating opportunity. Bitcoin network difficulty is about to retarget in 434 blocks (a small adjustment of 1.1 percent), a neutral sign that mining hash is steady despite lower volatility in realized price.

Watch for three signals that would alter this read. First, a recapture and hold above the 200-day line by Bitcoin or Ethereum, which would mark the first regime change in the data. Second, a reversal in whale flows from off-exchange to on-exchange, which would signal the accumulation phase is ending. Third, a shift in funding from positive back to negative across Ethereum, SOL, and DOGE, which would suggest the long-heavy leverage is cooling; today it is running hot and at rising cost. Until one of these conditions flips, the tape reads as capitulation in sentiment with selective accumulation in fact, a setup that neither confirms a crash nor permits a sustainable rally.
